paragraphs: OpenAI. On Tuesday, November 17, OpenAI released two models in the GPT-6.2 family. Astra is the larger one, built for hard, multi-step work. Sol is the smaller one, meant for fast and cheap jobs. Both are in ChatGPT Work and Codex for Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu plans, and Enterprise and Edu need an admin to turn them on. Developers can call them in the API as gpt-6.2-astra and gpt-6.2-sol. Astra costs $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, which OpenAI says is 20% below GPT-6 Astra. Sol costs $2 and $10.

The performance claims are OpenAI's own. It says Astra beats GPT-6 Astra by 5.2 points on its Agents' Last Exam benchmark at under a third of the cost, and beats Fable 5.2 by 5.5 points at about 5% of the cost. OpenAI also notes the Fable 5.2 result leaves out nine tasks that ran on a fallback model, which matters when you compare. On a 3D benchmark it lists Astra at 1,318 Elo against 1,271 for Fable 5.2. The launch also carries a safety note: OpenAI calls Astra its first public model at the "High" level for AI self-improvement.
stories.means: The useful idea for marketing teams is the two-size pairing: use the big model only when the job is hard, and a small one for routine work. Lower prices also tend to show up later in the tools marketers use. Treat the benchmark wins as a claim until outside testers repeat them. That is our read, and we have not tried either model.
stories.clip: Make a two-column list of your marketing AI tasks: "needs deep thinking" and "just needs to be fast." A campaign brief might go in the first column, and tidying a content calendar in the second. Next time, notice which column your AI tool treats each task as.
deeper: Cached input is cheaper: $0.40 per million tokens for Astra and $0.10 for Sol, per OpenAI.
OpenAI says Sol is within 0.5 points of Astra on its FrontierCode 2.0 test at about one fifth of the cost. That is also a vendor figure.
OpenAI says both models meet its Critical cyber and High biology and chemistry levels, so they ship with tighter safeguards.
In two tests the models more often failed to mention blockers, so OpenAI added instructions in Codex. It is a good reminder to ask AI tools to report what went wrong.
stories.sources: OpenAI announcement (primary source, vendor-reported). We read one primary source only.

stories.headline: Nvidia beats estimates, and its board says Huang will not be reinstated
stories.teaser_title: Nvidia beats estimates, and its board says it does not plan to bring Huang back as CEO.
stories.teaser_line: Revenue of about $115.8 billion, and a higher growth forecast.
paragraphs: Markets. Yesterday's issue noted that Nvidia was about to report earnings. The results are now in. Nvidia reported on Tuesday, its first results since Jensen Huang resigned as CEO last week. Per CNBC, adjusted earnings were $2.68 a share against $2.48 expected, and revenue was $115.84 billion against $109.10 billion expected, more than double the $57 billion of a year earlier. Data center revenue was $107.6 billion. The company guided to about $130 billion next quarter against $125.1 billion expected, and the stock rose more than 3% after hours.

On the leadership question, board chair Harvey Jones said on the call that the board "does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO." Interim CEO Colette Kress called it "business as usual." She also raised next year's growth outlook to 75% from 70%. On China, Nvidia said its outlook assumes no data center compute revenue from China. It also said major AI labs should make up about 15% of data center sales this year. Those are company statements, and the stock reaction can change by morning.
stories.means: Spending on AI infrastructure is still growing fast, even after a shock at the top. For marketers, that suggests AI vendors and AI features will keep competing for attention and budget. One quarter is not a trend, so treat this as one data point. That is our reading, not investment advice.
stories.clip: Write a three-sentence explanation of "beat expectations" for a coworker who does not follow stocks. Use the numbers above: what was expected, what happened, and why the gap matters. It is good practice for turning a dense report into a clear social post.
deeper: Data center revenue beat the Street Account estimate of $101.87 billion, per CNBC.
China is the main risk CNBC highlights, after a Commerce Department rule on remote access to chips.
We read CNBC's live coverage in full. The Yahoo Finance live blog is a second outlet, and we saw only its headline and summary.
stories.sources: CNBC (read in full), Yahoo Finance live blog (headline and summary only)

stories.headline: LeBron James sues an AI betting app over an ad he says copied his likeness
stories.teaser_title: LeBron James sues an AI betting app over an ad he says copied his likeness.
stories.teaser_line: A live test case for AI likeness in advertising.
paragraphs: Advertising. LeBron James filed a lawsuit in federal court in Manhattan on Tuesday against an AI sports betting app called Bron, its parent company PlayVision, and its two co-founders. His complaint says an AI-made ad showed a figure with his tattoos, his number 23 jersey and a simulated version of his voice scrolling through betting options. It says the ad drew about one million views on X in a day. He accuses the company of using the "Bron" name to suggest he endorsed the app, and he asks for damages and a court order stopping it.

According to CNBC, the startup took the ad down from X and Instagram after a cease-and-desist letter on November 5, and says it is working to change the app's name. The complaint argues the company knew publicity would outweigh legal risk. These are the plaintiff's allegations, and no court has ruled. Separately, a press-release survey commissioned by a research company says 43% of Americans have felt tricked by an AI ad, and more than half do not trust AI-advertised products to match their descriptions. We read an excerpt only of that release.
stories.means: For anyone making ads, the line is simple: do not copy a real person's face, voice or nickname without written permission. This case may become a reference point for how courts treat AI likeness in marketing. The survey is a sponsored company's own study, so use it as a hint about trust, not a fact about all consumers. That is our view, not legal advice.
stories.clip: Write four rules for how your team uses AI in marketing work. For example: no real people's likeness without permission, label AI-made images, keep a record of prompts, and check every claim. Save it as a short page anyone on the team can find.
deeper: The complaint was filed in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York, per CNBC.
It also says the company treated the alleged violation as a marketing expense, which is the plaintiff's framing.
The survey was commissioned from Talker Research by Auros (formerly UserTesting). We read the press release excerpt, not the full study, and it is not independent.
We did not read the complaint itself, only CNBC's report of it.
stories.sources: CNBC (news report), PR Newswire release via Morningstar (company-commissioned survey, excerpt only)

newai.title: Microsoft launches seven MAI models, with big cost claims
paragraphs: At its Ignite event, Microsoft introduced seven of its own models. They cover coding, security, image editing, speech and routing. MAI Code 2 is for everyday company coding, and MAI Code 2 Flash is for small jobs like explaining code and quick fixes. MAI Image 2.7 handles image editing and generation, and MAI Realtime 1 is its first speech-to-speech model, starting at $0.01 per audio minute.

Where to get it: MAI Code 2 Flash is in GitHub Copilot and in limited preview in Microsoft Foundry. We could not confirm where the others are available. The catch: the comparisons, such as 98% of one rival's coding score at about 40% of the price, are Microsoft's own, relayed by one outlet. Good for: seeing that big software companies now build their own models, not only resell others. We have not tested any of them.

newai.title: Tasks in Gemini is now free in six countries
paragraphs: Google says its Gemini assistant can handle errands such as booking appointments, calling businesses and buying items, using a person's email, calendar and payment methods. It is free across the U.S., Japan, Korea, Canada, Australia and India, with the advanced features starting in the U.S. Users can set a spending limit upfront. Calling is not available in five U.S. states, including Indiana and Minnesota.
Good for: small errands. The catch: it needs access to personal accounts, so read the permissions first.

newai.title: Gemini Notebook can turn notes into a working site
paragraphs: In Google's Gemini Notebook, type "make me a site" in a notebook's chat and describe what it should do. PPC Land says it can produce things like explainers, dashboards and trackers from the sources in that notebook. It is rolling out on the web for users 18 and older, including Workspace accounts, with mobile "coming soon." Price and limits are not stated.
Good for: quick one-page campaign mockups. Check every result, since Google warns it can make mistakes.

connectors.title: No new connectors, but Claude Desktop adds a release channel choice
paragraphs: Connectors are add-ons that let Claude, Anthropic's AI assistant, work with other apps. Claude's release notes show no new connector news today. The one new entry, dated November 17, lets users of Claude Desktop, its computer app, choose a release channel.
Stable is the default, and Latest gets updates about once a day, which can mean newer features and more rough edges. Check the tool's own setup page for steps.

connectors.title: Tip: turn a content calendar into a to-do list
paragraphs: Paste your content calendar into any AI chat tool and ask: "Count how many posts are planned this week, list any with no owner or no due date, and draft a one-line reminder for each. Show me the list before you change anything."
How you might use it: it turns a busy calendar into a short to-do list. Asking to see the list first lets you catch mistakes before you rely on it. Remove names and private details before you paste.
connectors.sources: A tip with no outside claim.

prompt.title: Tell the AI what a good answer looks like
prompt.intro: Before you ask for a draft, write the rules a good answer must follow. This is a general prompting habit that follows Anthropic's advice to be clear and direct. The exact layout below is our own version.
prompt.weak: Write a campaign brief for this product launch.
prompt.strong:
Write a one-page campaign brief for the product below.

Product: [paste a short description]
About the campaign: [3 short bullets: the audience, the main goal, the budget or timing]

A good brief will:
1. Stay under 250 words.
2. Open with one specific reason this audience should care, not "We are excited to announce."
3. Connect two of my bullets to two concrete actions for the team.
4. Sound confident: plain words, no buzzwords.
5. End with one clear next step.

If any rule cannot be met with what I gave you, tell me what is missing instead of making something up.

why.title: The target is clear
why.text: The AI knows what "good" means before it writes, so it stops guessing.

why.title: Easy to judge
why.text: You can check the draft against five rules instead of going by feel.

why.title: Specific, not generic
why.text: Rules that tie your bullets to real actions push out empty filler.

why.title: Gaps get flagged
why.text: The last line asks for what is missing, so it will not invent details.

prompt.try: Pick one real product or campaign. Run the prompt with your three bullets, then check the draft against each rule. Change one rule, for example the word limit, and run it again to see what shifts. About 5 minutes.
prompt.sources: Anthropic prompting best practices (general advice on being clear and direct). We did not find one page that names this exact technique, so the rule list format is our own adaptation.

brief.name: $5B for AI drug design
brief.text: Isomorphic Labs announced a $5 billion Series C on November 17, led by Greenoaks and Sequoia Capital. It says the money will go to its simulation models and moving drug candidates toward clinical trials. It follows a $2.1 billion Series B. No valuation was stated.

brief.name: AI Mode cuts clicks
brief.text: A preprint field test of 1,100 U.S. Google users found that moving to Google's AI Mode cut clicks to websites by 18.8 percentage points. It has not been peer reviewed, and the sample skews young, educated and Democratic.

brief.name: AppLovin eyes Criteo
brief.text: Reuters reports, citing sources, that AppLovin is among firms in talks to buy ad tech company Criteo. Criteo declined to comment, and no deal is announced. We read a preview only of the story.
